## TS-001 · Actuation and power architecture

**Question.** Which actuation and power architecture should SUS-M1 baseline?

Status **in-work** · decision authority lead · weights draft (DQ-016) · decisions DQ-006, DQ-016

Joint actuation of the walker and the power source that goes with it. Two power alternatives are analysed side by side until this study closes (decision DQ-006); alternative B is split by joint actuator type because the two respond differently to faults local to one joint. The pilot station, locomotion and UAV dock are other studies (TS-002 to TS-004).

### Alternatives

| ID | Alternative | Description | Elements | Specific hazards |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Centralised hydraulic | An engine-driven hydraulic power unit with accumulators feeds valve-controlled cylinders at every joint through a common pressure line; pilot-operated check valves hold the joints when pressure is lost. | SUS-M1-PWR-HPU, SUS-M1-PWR-DIST | HAZ-PWR-001 |
| B-EHA | Series-hybrid with electrohydraulic joints | An engine-generator and a battery feed a DC bus; every joint has a self-contained electrohydraulic actuator (motor, pump, local reservoir and cylinder) with its own holding valves. | SUS-M1-PWR-GEN, SUS-M1-PWR-BAT, SUS-M1-PWR-DIST | HAZ-PWR-002, HAZ-PWR-003 |
| B-EMA | Series-hybrid with electromechanical joints | The same DC bus feeds electric motors with gearboxes or roller screws at every joint; spring-applied brakes hold the joints when power is lost. | SUS-M1-PWR-GEN, SUS-M1-PWR-BAT, SUS-M1-PWR-DIST | HAZ-PWR-002, HAZ-PWR-003 |

### Evidence

| ID | Criteria | Kind | Status | Source or need | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TS-001-E01 | C09 | simulation | done | `sim/results/ts001-fault-response.md` | With load holding working, every supply-loss mode is safe across the envelope at level 2 (level 1 tips 14-19 of 180 cases through its unsized centre-of-pressure limit, A3). With load holding failed, a hydraulic supply loss (A) and an isolated battery (B, SYS-014) are identical: torque goes to zero and the cockpit drops in 117 of 180 cases at up to 4.1 m/s (level 2). A bus undervoltage that keeps 35% of torque (B, assumed floor) drops it in 27 cases at up to 2.3 m/s, still above the 1.0 m/s safe drop speed. The alternatives differ by the torque left after the fault, not by the technology. |
| TS-001-E02 | C01, C06, C09 | analysis | done | `sim/results/sizing-cf4.md` | Every alternative must deliver ankle 26.5 kN m and knee 22.5 kN m at full supply, and at least 0.6 m g L_foot at the ankle when load holding engages (SYS-016); this sets the actuator class for C01 and C06 and the torque-supply curve each alternative must show for C09. |

| TS-001-E04 | C02, C11 | simulation | planned | Actuator models from TS-001-E03 data; a level-2 actuator layer between the controller and the joint torques. | Level-2 walker with actuator dynamics (bandwidth, backlash, compliance) per alternative. |

| TS-001-E06 | C09 | analysis | planned | Failure modes and rates of the holding devices (FMECA, Task 205 inputs) and a level-2 single-joint fault mode. | Fault modes local to one joint (electrohydraulic actuator leak, motor winding fault, brake failure) and the reliability of the holding device of each alternative: pilot-operated check valves (A, B-EHA) against spring-applied brakes (B-EMA). |

### Assumptions

- Concept stage; no hardware is selected and no vendor data has been obtained.
- Joint torques as adopted in the level-2 spec (ankle 26.5 kN m, knee 22.5 kN m; DQ-012) apply to every alternative: the actuators are sized to the walker, not the walker to the actuators.
- At simulation fidelity the alternatives differ only in how joint torque falls when supply is lost (the capacity curve in sim/plant/walker.py); actuator dynamics and faults local to one joint are not modelled.

Requirements waiting on this study: SYS-007, SYS-009, SYS-014, SYS-015, SYS-016.

### Open actions

- Confirm or change the criteria weights (decision DQ-016)
- Obtain the vendor data for TS-001-E03; it unblocks TS-001-E04 and TS-001-E05
- Test whether the residual bus floor (assumed 35% in sim/spec/walker.yaml) is credible for the series-hybrid bus; the C09 difference between A and B rests on it
- Score the remaining criteria from evidence, then set the study to ready-for-decision for the lead
